# `equal_null`

<!-- @generated by `cargo xtask docs-sql`; do not edit. -->

Returns same result as the EQUAL(=) operator for non-null operands,
but returns true if both are null, false if one of the them is null.

**Applies to:** Krishiv 0.2.0 and above. Spark: 3.5 and later.

## Syntax

```text
equal_null(expr1, expr2)
```

## Details

| | |
|---|---|
| Krishiv | Implemented |
| Group | `predicate_funcs` |
| Kind | scalar (function) |
| Added in Spark | 3.4.0 |
| In Spark profiles | 3.5 and later |
| Arguments | 2 |
| Deterministic | yes |

## Examples

```sql
-- equal_null, example 1
> SELECT equal_null(3, 3);
true
```

```sql
-- equal_null, example 2
> SELECT equal_null(1, '11');
false
```

```sql
-- equal_null, example 3
> SELECT equal_null(true, NULL);
false
```

```sql
-- equal_null, example 4
> SELECT equal_null(NULL, 'abc');
false
```

```sql
-- equal_null, example 5
> SELECT equal_null(NULL, NULL);
true
```

## Version history

- Added in Spark 3.4.0.
- Added in Krishiv 0.2.0.
